# Intel Graphics Software Engineer Interview Experience

Last Updated : 24 Apr, 2019

I had a phone interview, then an onsite interview at Intel in Folsom, California, for the position of Graphics Software Engineer. They mostly asked questions about C++.
**Round 1: Phone interview**
-Tell me about yourself
-What is a template in C++
-How would you resolve an issue within a group when working on a group project
**Round 2: Onsite interview**
-Asked questions about resume and projects
-Why are you interested in this position
-Difference between stack and heap
-What is an inline function
-What is a virtual function and why is it needed
-What is virtual memory
-Difference between array and linked list
-What is a page fault
-How do you set the last 2 bits in a number?
-Why do we need to use templates
-What is the difference between a class and a struct?
-Question about access modifiers
Here are some tips for you:
-Go over your resume often
-Review C++ concepts and operating systems concepts
-Review data structures such as arrays and linked lists

sources.passage:
. 

**Second Technnical Phone Screen (1 hour) :**
Two Questions on Data Structures and Algorithms were asked : 
1. Linked List Cycle - https://leetcode.com/problems/linked-list-cycle/
2. Binary Tree Level Order Traversal II - https://leetcode.com/problems/binary-tree-level-order-traversal-ii/

Apart from those questions, I was asked to explain couple of projects that I had done during my Masters. 
And was asked to briefly explain OO Design of the Tic-Tac-Toe game. 

One week after this I was asked to schedule on-site interview. 

**Onsite(3 Rounds)** : 
Round 1 (45 mins) : 
I was asked to explain one project from my Masters. I was asked to write class diagrams and thoroughly explain the flow. 
Two Questions on Data Structures and Algorithms were asked: 
1. Pow(x, n) - https://leetcode.com/problems/powx-n/
2. A diagram of a typical theater room was shown (with all chairs and people sitting on few of the chairs) and asked to simulate moving from one location to another, but should pass minimum number of people on the way. 

Round 2 (45 mins): 
First 20 mins, few technical questions on differences between C and C++, C++ and Java, and features that I like in C++11 was asked. 

Coding Question:
1. A string representing a students daily attendance was given (A - absent, L - Late, P - Present), and was certain conditions were given(he shouldn't be absent for 2 consecutive days and he should not be late for more than 3 days), if those conditions were met, the student would get into trouble. 
2. The question was improvised for N days. Where N also represents length of each strings, ie., if N is two each string will be AP, PA, PP, AA.. etc. He was expecting a dynamic programming solution, and I gave him a recursive backtracking solution. But he was not satisfied. 

Round 3 (45 mins): 
This round was with the hiring manager. 
Behavioral Questions : 
1. Give me an example of a time you faced a conflict while working on a team. How did you handle that?
2. Tell me about a time you were under a lot of pressure. What was going on, and how did you get through it?

One coding question: 
1. Reverse nodes in k-group - https://leetcode.com/problems/reverse-nodes-in-k-group/

She also discussed about visa sponsorship, when can I join, and any offer deadlines and pending interviews with other companies. 

Result : Reject. No feedback as to why
